Subject: Re: Audit logs & data access — post-demo follow-up

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. 

FinCo's security policy asks that audit logs include the following minimum columns: timestamp (ISO8601), principal_email, principal_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, ip_address, outcome (success/fail), and request_id. We prefer CSV for ingestion into our SIEM, but a JSON-lines export is also useful for ad-hoc review.

A few clarifying questions:
- Can audit logs be exported for a specified date range and filtered by principal_role?
- How long are access logs retained by default? Is retention configurable at the tenant level?
- Do logs contain any request_payload or PII fields by default (we want to ensure we don't see customer PII in logs unless necessary)?

If you can provide a redacted sample (last 7 days) and the schema, that would be great. Also please attach any SOC2 or compliance summary you can share.

Samantha Jones
Director, Information Security
FinCo Bank

Hi Samantha / Marissa —

Attaching the requested artifacts: access-logs-sample.json (JSON-lines, redacted), audit-logs-schema.csv (header row only), and redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (one-page summary we can share). Quick answers inline below.

- Export formats: We support CSV exports (columnar) and JSON-lines. Exports can be scoped by date range and filtered by principal_role or principal_email.
- Retention: Default access-log retention is 90 days for hosted accounts. For Dedicated or Private deployments we support configurable retention policies and can set tenant-level retention down to 30 days or up to 7 years depending on contract.
- PII in logs: By default, we do not persist full request payloads or customer-submitted PII fields in access logs. Logs contain metadata (request_id, resource_id, user_id, internal_role, timestamp, ip_address) and a hashed payload reference (request_payload_hash). If customers enable request auditing, they can opt-in to include redacted payload fields; this is controlled via a tenant-level setting.
- Data residency & egress: For Private/VPC deployments exports can be run within the customer's network. For hosted accounts, we can provide export endpoints in-region (US, EU) and support signed-URL delivery to a customer-controlled bucket.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached sample and schema.
2) If everything looks fine, we can schedule a technical call to walk the sample and options for tenant-level retention and export automation.

Scheduling: Marissa, I propose Wed 3/31 at 10:00am PT for a short technical review. Sam, does that work?

Regards,
Aditya Rao
